purpose: Determine whether a verified binary operational dependency graph improves pre-action safety classification beyond highlighting the same evidence.

model.runtime: pinned bf16 merged fused CUDA; exact environment recorded per run

data.split_unit: scenario group including all safe/unsafe variants, paraphrases and shared templates
data.sampling: Balance safety classes and families at design time; report artificial prevalence. Do not select examples by model failure.
data.gold: Two independent annotations from visible prefixes, followed by adjudication before opening predictions. Preserve ambiguity and exclusions.
data.fallback: Without independent annotation, describe as programmatic mechanism diagnostics, never independent benchmark validation.
data.scope: This is a pilot, not a powered confirmatory benchmark. Freshness does not establish independence from model training.

annotation.edge_definition: Direct use of observed data, identifier, resource, state or implemented directive from an earlier event. Exclude shared topic, mere temporal adjacency and exclusively transitive use.
annotation.user_messages: Always retain all causally available user messages. The tested graph covers event-event dependencies; user/profile provenance is outside graph scope and must be reported.
annotation.unknowns: Do not force ambiguous edges or unobservable safety labels into binary gold; report coverage and sensitivity separately.

presentation: Choose exactly one generic renderer on development before unlocking pilot. Same safety question and observed history for all arms; record token-length differences.

metrics.primary: Pooled action-level AP on the prespecified annotated prefixes. All eligible negative prefixes are included. Report event-count strata because long trajectories contribute more pairs.
secondary: macro-trajectory AP on positive-containing trajectories with explicit coverage
metrics.aggregation: Pre-action labels scored directly. Max-over-actions versus trajectory gold is a separately labeled secondary analysis.
metrics.thresholds: Select each operational threshold on development once; report shared 0.5 as a diagnostic, never optimize on locked labels.

statistics.resampling_unit: scenario group; preserve all prefixes and paired variants together
statistics.multiplicity: Holm over the two prespecified primary hypothesis tests; other contrasts descriptive
statistics.minimum_useful_effect: Must be agreed and frozen before locked inference; proposed absolute AP gain 0.03, subject to pilot power review.
statistics.power: Use development group variation to size a separate confirmation set for 80% power; 60 locked pilot trajectories are not assumed sufficient.
statistics.equivalence: No equivalence claim without a prespecified margin and interval wholly inside that margin.

graph_corruption.constraints: Only temporally admissible edges; preserve observations. Report actual changed fraction and overlap; if no alternative exists mark structurally uninformative.
graph_corruption.locked_control: Choose and freeze one corruption specification before locked pilot. Other severity curves are development diagnostics.

gates: Reproduce archived metrics and exact causal renderer hashes before new model inference.
Freeze dataset hashes, scenario-group split, prompts, runtime and contrasts.
Complete annotation adjudication and audit label observability.
Validate baseline task suitability on development and run a small numerical/order repeat.
Agree minimum useful effect and freeze remaining draft choices.
If verified graph shows no useful advantage, investigate representation/model suitability before further LINK optimization.
If verified graph helps, evaluate short neutral NOUL with a development-only threshold, then independently confirm.
stopping: One locked pilot read. Any subsequent tuning consumes that set as development and requires another locked set.
